title: JANUS Egypt Evidence Map
purpose: Source-bound scientific map: claim -> source -> evidence class -> confidence -> contradiction/limit -> missing killer-test -> next action.

claims.claim: The 1902 Mendes burial contained CG 53469 / JE 35425 plus separate stamped-gold djed material, but the individual djed passport and exact body position remain unresolved.
claims.source: Griffith Institute TopBib/Cairo Museum material + Engelbach MSS; see master ledger Mendes branch.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: No recovered individual CG/JE identity or anatomical coordinate for the djed.
claims.missing_killer_test: Original Cairo Museum JE VI pp.486-487 plus linked gold-group register/photo/list.
claims.next_action: Request the exact JE pages and group documentation; keep Mendes separate from Tell Ibn Salam/Thmuis.

claims.claim: Bowdoin records a 1904 Cairo-to-New-York certificate naming 'Nahman & Co.', while Louvre independently records M. Nahman of Cairo in the 1905 provenance chain for E 11072.
claims.source: Bowdoin accession-file review + Louvre 1905 entry-book transcription; see master ledger.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: The two names are not yet bound to the same legal/business entity by letterhead, address, invoice or company record.
claims.missing_killer_test: 1904-1905 business record explicitly connecting 'Nahman & Co.' to Maurice Nahman.
claims.next_action: Use Brooklyn archive/library search as the entity-resolution gate.

claims.claim: Louvre E 11072 is documented as one component of a multipart stone apparatus, probably including a box/basin and base.
claims.source: Louvre 1905 entry-book description; see master ledger Louvre branch.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: Pre-museum archaeological findspot and any biological contents are not documented by the supplied record.
claims.missing_killer_test: Recover pre-1905 provenance, old photographs or matching detached components.
claims.next_action: Treat E 11072 as a comparative witness for multipart Osirian apparatus only.

claims.claim: Oxyrhynchus preserves multiple pseudo-Osirian burial spaces; Roman Gallery 2E niche 2 was found still closed.
claims.source: Maite Mascort source-bound excavation reply + thesis/publication route; see master ledger Oxyrhynchus branch.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: A closed niche does not automatically preserve each object's exact orientation after excavation documentation is lost or incomplete.
claims.missing_killer_test: Field plans/photos/notes preserving object-by-object positions in niche 2.
claims.next_action: Keep niche 2 as the strongest current closed-context gate.

claims.claim: Magic balls at Oxyrhynchus occur in the protective context of Osirian simulacra; many were inside small inscribed limestone boxes with pseudo-pyramidal lids, with about nine reportedly found closed.
claims.source: Maite Mascort reply + published material route; see master ledger.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: Protective function does not establish exact cardinal placement of every box; material wording must remain source-bound.
claims.missing_killer_test: Box-level linkage of field coordinate, inscription, ball and material analysis.
claims.next_action: Preserve object-level rather than generalized ritual reconstruction.

claims.claim: Niche-2 boxes crosswalk as 15307a/F343->O57, b/F344->O56, c/F345->O55, d/F346->O53, e/F347->O58, f/F348->O59; O54/F339 is a corridor control.
claims.source: Maite Mascort object mapping + Goyon article supplied by her.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: Object identity mapping is not physical orientation mapping.
claims.next_action: Keep O54 explicit as an external control.

claims.claim: Goyon's corpus supports an oriented protective tradition, but the six niche-2 boxes do not demonstrate a complete cardinal geometry.
claims.source: Goyon, Les inscriptions du petit mobilier funéraire, especially pp.197, 199-201, combined only with the verified niche-2 crosswalk.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: Mapped readings include south/west/east plus belonging/epithet statements, no clean full N/E/S/W set, and numeral uncertainty for part of the south group.
claims.missing_killer_test: Compare inscription direction with actual excavated box position/orientation.

claims.claim: Published material checked so far preserves the shared niche-2 lower-fill context but not usable individual in-situ coordinates/orientations for 15307a-f.
claims.source: Published fichas/thesis review followed by narrow expert query; see master ledger current Oxyrhynchus state.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: Unpublished field records may still preserve the missing geometry.
claims.missing_killer_test: Mission field notes/photos/plans showing positions and orientations before removal.

claims.claim: Cairo JE 37516 is interpreted by Christian Leitz as an actual Osirian germination/garden basin; the spout supports practical use, while direct residue/use-wear proof is absent.
claims.source: Christian Leitz source-bound reply regarding JE 37516.
claims.evidence_class: specialist interpretation tied to published object study
claims.contradiction_or_limit: No published residue, sediment or conservation analysis was identified; no direct link to a specific later burial/cache.
claims.missing_killer_test: Material/residue/use-wear study and complete object dossier.
claims.next_action: Use JE 37516 as the strongest current manufacture anchor, not as direct archaeometric proof of repeated use.

claims.claim: The Ehnasya published groups belong to one broader 1956 discovery recorded under common Record No. 26, with 56 Osiris statuettes plus other statue remains; identifiers such as 8/26-13/26 are later research identifiers.
claims.source: Mohamed Abdelbar summary based on museum-store documentation.
claims.evidence_class: specialist with record access / museum-record summary
claims.contradiction_or_limit: JANUS has not independently seen the original register image; individual present-day official inventory numbers remain unresolved.
claims.missing_killer_test: Authorized scan/certified transcription of Record No.26 and linked inspector/transfer material.
claims.next_action: Preserve the expert transcription as bounded evidence and keep the primary-record gate open.

claims.claim: The exact trench, depth, architecture and sealed-vs-dispersed status of the 1956 Ehnasya discovery remain unresolved in the documentation currently available to the specialist.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: A fuller original SCA/Antiquities Service file may preserve more detail.
claims.missing_killer_test: Original discovery/inspector/register dossier with spatial information.
claims.next_action: Do not call the find a closed cache unless a primary source establishes it.

claims.claim: Pitt Rivers specimen 1901.40.53 from Djer Tomb O was sampled for radiocarbon work in 2010, but the sampled portion is not identifiable from documentation and the museum file does not link the hair group to the famous bracelet-bearing forearm.
claims.source: Pitt Rivers collection-file and radiocarbon correspondence supplied to JANUS.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: Excavation cards may preserve more precise micro-context.
claims.missing_killer_test: Tomb O excavation cards/distribution records and original labels.
claims.next_action: Keep HAIR_TO_FOREARM_LINK = NOT_SUPPORTED without an explicit primary binding record.

claims.claim: Harvard's Giza Project does not hold a complete Osiris Shaft excavation archive; fuller notes/plans/photos remain in the Hawass excavation archive.
claims.source: Peter Der Manuelian / Harvard Giza Project reply.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: This is not a negative archaeological finding; it only defines where the archive is not complete.
claims.missing_killer_test: Access Hawass/SCA Level-3 excavation and object-register records.
claims.next_action: Do not infer documentary absence from Harvard's incomplete holdings.

claims.claim: The 1994 Giza Sokar-Osiris cemetery remains high-value but current correspondence has not resolved coffin/ball object associations or excavation geometry.
claims.source: Prof. Abdelrahman Ali reply referring the questions to SCA reports and Amal Samuel's dissertation.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: No primary 1994 report pages or dissertation sections have yet been obtained through this route.
claims.missing_killer_test: Excavation report/dissertation pages with tomb numbers, plans, photos and object associations.
claims.next_action: Keep open; do not promote secondary summary into object-level provenance.

claims.claim: British Museum guidance places P.BM EA 10688 verso 4-7 on frames 5-6, with Gardiner Hieratic Papyri Vol.2 as the control publication and BM Images as the high-resolution route.
claims.source: British Museum Egyptian Written Culture curator reply.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: Broader interpretation was not validated and exact frame-to-line alignment has not yet been replayed.
claims.missing_killer_test: Readable frames 5-6 aligned line-by-line against Gardiner.

claims.claim: For TR 30/1/24/8 and TR 3/2/24/5, SCA directed provenance/scientific-data access to Cairo Egyptian Museum while keeping formal object examination/publication as a separate SCA procedure.
claims.source: Supreme Council of Antiquities Permanent Committee reply.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: No content from the two TR entries has yet been obtained.
claims.missing_killer_test: Scans/transcriptions of the two entries with object-level cross-references.
claims.next_action: Proceed through Cairo Egyptian Museum and preserve the Thmuis/Mendes separation.

claims.claim: A 1956 Miguel Mujica Gallo catalogue already pictured an Egyptian dagger labelled with the cartouche of Tothmes III; another caption states that an Egyptian dagger had formed part of the Stouyvesant collection.
claims.source: Smithsonian Libraries scan of the 1956 catalogue.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: The historical pharaonic attribution is not independently validated and identity with the present Lima object still requires concordance.
claims.missing_killer_test: Visual/inventory match among the 1956 catalogue object, present Lima object and Stouyvesant documentation.
claims.next_action: Treat Stouyvesant as a provenance lead, not a completed chain.

claims.claim: Independent sites collectively support a real material sequence involving Osirian simulacrum manufacture, protective equipment/inscriptions and burial/deposition, but not one universal apparatus or geometry.
claims.source: Synthesis of Coptos, Oxyrhynchus and Ehnasya nodes only.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: No single site currently preserves an unbroken manufacture -> specific simulacrum -> protection set -> final burial chain; chronology and local practice differ.
claims.missing_killer_test: One site/context with object-level continuity across manufacture, simulacrum, protection assemblage and final deposition.
claims.next_action: Use as a research model only and preserve site-level independence.

claims.claim: No evidence currently obtained by JANUS establishes that an examined object or human remain is a literal physical body part of Osiris.
claims.source: Global synthesis of all current Egypt evidence nodes.
claims.contradiction_or_limit: This is an evidentiary verdict, not a metaphysical statement about religious tradition.
claims.missing_killer_test: Any such claim would require secure excavation provenance, chain of custody, direct material analysis, chronological compatibility and independent replication.
